name: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid
line: The Prophet's ﷺ first wife and the first person to believe in his message.
story: Khadijah was a respected merchant of Makkah who hired Muhammad ﷺ to lead her caravan, then proposed marriage. When he came down from Hira trembling, she wrapped him up and reassured him that Allah would never disgrace him. She spent her wealth on the cause and stood by him through the boycott. She was the mother of all his children but Ibrahim.
legacy: Jibril brought her greetings of peace from Allah and news of a house in Paradise.
lesson: Faith often begins with someone who believes in you first.
note: Her age of 40 at marriage is the best-known report; some historians give a younger age.

name: Sawdah bint Zam'ah
line: An early emigrant to Abyssinia who married the Prophet ﷺ after Khadijah's death.
story: Sawdah was among the first Muslims and emigrated to Abyssinia with her husband, who died after they returned. The Prophet ﷺ married her after Khadijah died, and she cared for his household and young daughters. She was known for her good humour. Later in life she gave her turn with the Prophet ﷺ to Aishah.
note: Her death year is disputed: late in Umar's caliphate or about 54 AH (674 CE).

name: Aishah bint Abi Bakr
line: Daughter of Abu Bakr, wife of the Prophet ﷺ and one of the greatest teachers of Islam.
story: Aishah grew up in a Muslim home and married the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah. When she was slandered, Allah cleared her name in verses of Surah al-Nur. The Prophet ﷺ died in her room, with his head on her lap. For nearly fifty years after, senior Companions came to her with questions of law, Quran and Sunnah.
legacy: Over two thousand hadith are narrated through her.
lesson: Patience under false accusation is answered by Allah in His time.
note: Her birth year is approximate. Some give her death as 57 AH.

name: Hafsah bint Umar
line: Daughter of Umar, who guarded the first written collection of the Quran.
story: Hafsah was widowed when her husband Khunays died of wounds from the early battles, and the Prophet ﷺ married her in 625. She could read and write and was known for fasting and night prayer. The sheets of the Quran gathered under Abu Bakr passed to her, and Uthman borrowed them to make the copies he sent across the empire.
legacy: Every standard Quran today goes back to the sheets she kept.
note: Her death year is given as 41 or 45 AH.

name: Zaynab bint Khuzaymah
line: Called Umm al-Masakin, Mother of the Poor, she died only months after her marriage.
story: Zaynab was known even before Islam for feeding the poor, earning the name Umm al-Masakin. Widowed by the early battles, she married the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah. She died a few months later, the only wife besides Khadijah to die in his lifetime.
lesson: A name earned by generosity outlives a short life.
when: Married about 625 CE; died months later
note: Historians differ on whether her previous husband died at Badr or Uhud.

name: Umm Salamah
line: A widow of great wisdom whose advice saved the day at Hudaybiyyah.
story: Hind, known as Umm Salamah, migrated to Abyssinia and then to Madinah, where she was separated from her husband and child for a year. When Abu Salamah died, she said the prayer the Prophet ﷺ taught for loss, and Allah gave her someone better: the Prophet ﷺ himself. At Hudaybiyyah, when the Companions hesitated, she advised him to shave his head first, and they all followed.
legacy: She was the last of the Mothers of the Believers to die.
lesson: Say the prayer for loss and trust Allah to replace what was taken.
note: Her separation story is from Ibn Ishaq; the Hudaybiyyah advice is in al-Bukhari. She died in 61 or 62 AH.

name: Zaynab bint Jahsh
line: The Prophet's ﷺ cousin, whose marriage to him was ordained in the Quran.
story: Zaynab was the Prophet's ﷺ cousin and was first married to his adopted son Zayd ibn Harithah. After their divorce, Allah revealed that the Prophet ﷺ should marry her, ending the old Arab custom that treated adopted sons as real sons. She would say Allah had married her from above the seven heavens. She worked with her hands and gave it all away.
legacy: The Prophet ﷺ said the first of his wives to follow him would be the one with the longest hand; it was Zaynab, the most generous.
note: The marriage year is given as 4 or 5 AH. The "longest hand" hadith is reported by Muslim.

name: Juwayriyah bint al-Harith
line: A chief's daughter whose marriage freed a hundred families of her tribe.
story: Juwayriyah was the daughter of the chief of Banu al-Mustaliq, taken captive after a battle. The Prophet ﷺ paid her ransom and married her. The Companions then freed their captives from her tribe, saying they were now the Prophet's ﷺ in-laws. Aishah said no woman was a greater blessing to her people.
legacy: She is remembered in a famous dhikr the Prophet ﷺ taught her after her long morning prayers.
note: The account of her people being freed is reported by Abu Dawud and Ahmad. Her death is given as 50 or 56 AH.

name: Umm Habibah
line: Daughter of Abu Sufyan who held to Islam in Abyssinia while her father led Makkah against it.
story: Ramlah, known as Umm Habibah, emigrated to Abyssinia. There her husband left Islam, but she held firm, alone in a foreign land. The Prophet ﷺ proposed to her by letter, and the Najashi conducted the marriage on his behalf. When her father Abu Sufyan, still a pagan, visited Madinah, she folded away the Prophet's ﷺ mat so he could not sit on it.
note: The hadith above is her narration of the twelve daily sunnah prayers. The mat story is from Ibn Sa'd. She died about 44 AH.

name: Safiyyah bint Huyayy
line: A Jewish noblewoman of Khaybar, freed and married by the Prophet ﷺ.
story: Safiyyah was the daughter of Huyayy, chief of Banu al-Nadir, captured at Khaybar. The Prophet ﷺ freed her and married her, making her freedom her dowry. When others teased her about her origins, he told her to say: my father is Harun, my uncle is Musa, and my husband is Muhammad ﷺ.
lesson: Lineage from the prophets is an honour, never a shame.
note: The freedom-as-dowry report is in al-Bukhari and Muslim; the Harun saying is reported by al-Tirmidhi. Her death is given as 50 or 52 AH.

name: Maymunah bint al-Harith
line: The last woman the Prophet ﷺ married, aunt of Ibn Abbas and Khalid ibn al-Walid.
story: Maymunah married the Prophet ﷺ at Sarif, near Makkah, after the make-up Umrah of 629. She was the last of his marriages. Her nephew Ibn Abbas often stayed in her home, which is how he came to see the Prophet's ﷺ night prayer. Decades later she died at Sarif, where she had married.
note: Her death is given as 51 AH by most historians; others say later.

name: Maria al-Qibtiyyah
line: An Egyptian woman sent by the ruler of Egypt, mother of the Prophet's ﷺ son Ibrahim.
story: Maria was a Coptic Christian from Egypt, sent to the Prophet ﷺ as a gift by al-Muqawqis in reply to his letter. She accepted Islam and lived in Madinah. In 630 she gave birth to Ibrahim, his only child not born to Khadijah, who died as a baby. She died in Madinah during Umar's caliphate.
legacy: The Prophet ﷺ urged kindness to the people of Egypt because of their ties of kinship.
note: Most scholars say she was the Prophet's ﷺ concubine and mother of his child (umm walad), not formally one of the Mothers of the Believers; some say he married her. Some commentators link 66:1 to her.

name: Rayhanah bint Zayd
line: A woman of the Jewish tribes of Madinah who joined the Prophet's ﷺ household.
story: Rayhanah was from the Jewish tribes of Madinah and was taken captive in 627. She later accepted Islam and lived in the Prophet's ﷺ household. She died before him, on his return from the Farewell Hajj according to some reports.
note: Historians differ on whether she was a wife or a concubine, and on whether she was of Banu Qurayzah or Banu al-Nadir. Little about her is firmly known.

name: al-Qasim ibn Muhammad
line: The Prophet's ﷺ first child, who died young and gave him the name Abu al-Qasim.
story: Al-Qasim was the first child of Muhammad ﷺ and Khadijah, born in Makkah before the revelation. He died as a small child. The Prophet ﷺ was known ever after as Abu al-Qasim, the father of al-Qasim.
when: Born about 598 CE; died in early childhood
note: His exact birth and death years are not known.

name: Zaynab bint Muhammad
line: Eldest daughter of the Prophet ﷺ, who ransomed her husband with her mother's necklace.
story: Zaynab married her cousin Abu al-As before Islam. When he was captured at Badr fighting for Quraysh, she sent Khadijah's necklace to ransom him, and the Prophet ﷺ was moved to tears. She then emigrated to Madinah. Abu al-As later accepted Islam and they were reunited, but she died in 629.
legacy: Her children were Ali and Umamah.
note: The necklace story is reported by Abu Dawud.

name: Ruqayyah bint Muhammad
line: Daughter of the Prophet ﷺ who emigrated twice with her husband Uthman.
story: Ruqayyah married Uthman ibn Affan and emigrated with him to Abyssinia, then to Madinah. She fell gravely ill as the Muslims marched to Badr, so the Prophet ﷺ told Uthman to stay and nurse her. She died in 624, as news of the victory reached Madinah.

name: Umm Kulthum bint Muhammad
line: Daughter of the Prophet ﷺ who married Uthman after her sister's death.
story: After Ruqayyah died, the Prophet ﷺ married her sister Umm Kulthum to Uthman, who was then called Dhu al-Nurayn, the possessor of two lights. She died in 630, and the Prophet ﷺ sat by her grave with tears in his eyes.
note: The grave scene is reported by al-Bukhari; commentators identify the daughter as Umm Kulthum.

name: Fatimah al-Zahra
role: Leader of the women of Paradise
line: The Prophet's ﷺ youngest daughter, wife of Ali and mother of Hasan and Husayn.
story: Fatimah grew up through the years of persecution, once wiping filth off her father's back at the Kaaba. She married Ali ibn Abi Talib and lived simply, grinding grain until her hands blistered. When she asked for a servant, the Prophet ﷺ taught her a dhikr instead. She died six months after him, the first of his family to follow him.
legacy: The Prophet's ﷺ descendants all come through her.
lesson: The Prophet ﷺ gave his dearest a better gift than ease: remembrance of Allah.
note: Her birth year is disputed (around 605 or 615 CE). Muslim 2424 is the hadith of the cloak, recited with 33:33; linking 3:61 to her family is reported by Muslim.

name: Abdullah ibn Muhammad
line: A son of the Prophet ﷺ and Khadijah who died as a baby in Makkah.
story: Abdullah, also called al-Tayyib and al-Tahir, was born to Muhammad ﷺ and Khadijah and died in infancy. Some of Quraysh mocked the Prophet ﷺ as "cut off", with no son to carry his name. The commentators say Surah al-Kawthar was revealed in reply: it is his enemy who is cut off.
note: Some historians count al-Tayyib and al-Tahir as separate sons; most say they are names of Abdullah. Whether he was born before or after the revelation is disputed.

name: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad
line: The Prophet's ﷺ last child, whose death taught that eclipses are signs, not omens.
story: Ibrahim was born to Maria in Madinah in 630 and died at about eighteen months. The Prophet ﷺ wept and said, "The eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, but we say only what pleases our Lord." The sun eclipsed that day and people said it was for Ibrahim. He corrected them: the sun and moon do not eclipse for anyone's death or life.
lesson: Grief is not weakness, and truth matters even in grief.

name: Hasan ibn Ali
line: The Prophet's ﷺ eldest grandson, who gave up power to unite the Muslims.
story: Hasan was born in Madinah to Fatimah and Ali. The Prophet ﷺ carried him on his shoulders and said this son of his was a leader through whom Allah might reconcile two great groups of Muslims. After Ali was killed, Hasan was pledged as caliph, then handed rule to Muawiyah in 661 to end the bloodshed. The year became known as the Year of Unity.
legacy: A prophecy fulfilled: peace chosen over power.
lesson: Giving up what is yours to stop bloodshed is greatness.
note: Tirmidhi 3768: Hasan and Husayn are the leaders of the youth of Paradise. His death year is given as 49 or 50 AH.

name: Husayn ibn Ali
line: The Prophet's ﷺ grandson, killed with his family at Karbala in 680.
story: Husayn grew up in the Prophet's ﷺ arms and was called one of the two leaders of the youth of Paradise. After Muawiyah's death he refused to pledge to Yazid and set out for Kufa. At Karbala his small party was surrounded, and on the 10th of Muharram, 61 AH, he and many of his family were killed.
legacy: Muslims of every school mourn Karbala as one of history's great wrongs.
lesson: Some stands are made knowing the cost.
when: Born 626 CE; killed 10 Muharram 61 AH (680 CE)
note: His birth year (4 AH) is approximate; the date of his death is firm.

name: Umamah bint Abi al-As
line: The granddaughter the Prophet ﷺ carried on his shoulder while he led the prayer.
story: Umamah, daughter of Zaynab, was carried by the Prophet ﷺ as he prayed: he set her down when he bowed and picked her up when he stood. After Fatimah's death, Ali married her, as Fatimah had wished.
lesson: Prayer and tenderness to children are not opposites.
note: Fatimah's wish that Ali marry her is reported by the historians.

name: Ali ibn Abi al-As
line: Zaynab's son, said to have ridden behind the Prophet ﷺ into Makkah.
story: Ali was the son of Zaynab and Abu al-As. Reports say the Prophet ﷺ seated him behind him on his mount at the conquest of Makkah. He died young.
note: Little is known for certain: some say he died as a boy in the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime, others that he was killed at Yarmuk.

name: Abdullah ibn Uthman
line: Son of Ruqayyah and Uthman, who died as a young child.
story: Abdullah was born to Ruqayyah and Uthman ibn Affan, probably in Abyssinia, and Uthman took the name Abu Abdullah from him. He died at about six, a few years after his mother.
note: Details of his birth and age at death come from the historians and vary.

name: Zaynab bint Ali
line: Granddaughter of the Prophet ﷺ who survived Karbala and spoke out for its victims.
story: Zaynab, daughter of Fatimah and Ali, married her cousin Abdullah ibn Jafar. She travelled with her brother Husayn to Karbala and saw him and her sons killed. She cared for the surviving women and children as captives were taken to Kufa and Damascus, and the historians record her bold speeches there.
lesson: Steadfastness can speak louder than an army.
when: Born about 627 CE; died about 682 CE
note: Her burial place is disputed: Damascus, Cairo and Madinah are all named. The wording of her speeches comes from later historians.

name: Umm Kulthum bint Ali
line: Granddaughter of the Prophet ﷺ who, according to Sunni sources, married Umar ibn al-Khattab.
story: Umm Kulthum was the younger daughter of Ali and Fatimah. Sunni sources report that Umar ibn al-Khattab asked for her hand to be joined by marriage to the Prophet's ﷺ family, and that she bore him a son, Zayd. She and Zayd are said to have died on the same day.
note: Her marriage to Umar is reported in Sunni sources; Shia scholars dispute it. Her dates are not known.

name: Ali Zayn al-Abidin
line: Husayn's son, who survived Karbala and became famed for worship and charity.
story: Ali ibn al-Husayn was too ill to fight at Karbala and survived. He returned to Madinah and devoted his life to prayer, earning the name Zayn al-Abidin. It is said that after he died, people found he had secretly carried food to a hundred poor households at night. Sunni scholars such as al-Zuhri praised his knowledge and character.
legacy: The Prophet's ﷺ line through Husayn continues through him.
note: His death year is given as 94 or 95 AH. A collection of prayers, al-Sahifa al-Sajjadiyya, is attributed to him.

name: Fatimah bint Asad
line: Wife of Abu Talib and mother of Ali, who cared for the orphan Muhammad ﷺ.
story: Fatimah bint Asad was the wife of Abu Talib and mother of Ali, Jafar and Aqil. When the young Muhammad ﷺ came to live in Abu Talib's house, she cared for him like her own. She accepted Islam and emigrated to Madinah, and when she died the Prophet ﷺ honoured her at her burial.
note: She is also counted among the female Companions. Reports that he shrouded her in his own shirt have chains of differing strength.

name: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah
line: A son of Ali known for his knowledge and strength, who stayed out of the civil wars.
story: Muhammad was Ali's son by Khawlah of Banu Hanifah, hence his name. He fought beside his father and was known for learning and great strength. In the later civil wars he stayed apart from both sides, and after much pressure pledged to the Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik.
note: He is not a descendant of Fatimah. Some groups after him claimed he was a hidden imam; he did not make that claim. His death is given as 81 AH.

name: Sukaynah bint al-Husayn
line: Husayn's daughter, a child at Karbala, later famed for her wit and love of poetry.
story: Sukaynah was a young girl at Karbala and among the survivors taken to Damascus. She grew up in Madinah, where she became known for her intelligence and for gathering poets and judging their verse.
note: Many stories about her literary gatherings come from later literary works and are of uncertain reliability.

name: Fatimah bint al-Husayn
line: Husayn's daughter, who survived Karbala and passed on hadith to later generations.
story: Fatimah was with her father at Karbala and survived. She married her cousin Hasan ibn Hasan and lived in Madinah, where she narrated hadith from her family and was trusted by the scholars of hadith.
note: Her death year is approximate (around 110 AH).

name: Zayd ibn Ali
line: Great-grandson of Ali who rose against the Umayyads in Kufa and was killed.
story: Zayd, son of Ali Zayn al-Abidin, was a scholar of Madinah. In 740 he led an uprising in Kufa against the Umayyad governor, but most of his supporters deserted him and he was killed in battle.
legacy: The Zaydi school, still followed in Yemen, takes its name from him.
note: Reports that Abu Hanifah supported his uprising are found in the historians.
